purpose: Select fonts and Jianying flower-text effects from semantic role, genre, frame conditions, and local resource availability. Use automatically for styled talking-head captions and overlays.

interpretation: Custom font choice is part of the base visual identity, not an optional finishing touch.
Ordinary talking-head templates use flower text sparsely; high-packaging edits use it more often but still on selected overlays rather than every spoken subtitle.
Font switching and flower text are separate decisions. A keyword may change font without receiving effectStyle, and flower text still needs a compatible font hierarchy.

automatic_selection_pipeline: Inspect the existing draft's fonts, canvas, speaker position, subtitle area, and resolvable local font/effect resources.
Classify each spoken beat as body, hook, identity, keyword, conflict, proof_or_number, method_step, turn, quote, result, CTA, emotion, or annotation.
Choose one base font, one display font, and only when justified one numeric_or_latin font. Do not exceed three font families in one video.
Keep continuous spoken subtitles in the base font. Switch only short overlays or partial keyword ranges to the display or numeric font.
Decide flower text after font role, color, size, position, and motion. Use it only when it adds a semantic function that plain typography cannot carry as clearly.
Resolve the complete source effect material and local resource path. If unresolved, fall back to font, fill, stroke, shadow, background, and portable keyframes.
Audit density, repeated effect IDs, collisions, and readability before saving.

display_viral.traits: Large counterforms and strong silhouette for short phrases.

display_playful.traits: Rounded, lively, tolerant of bounce motion.

numeric_or_latin.traits: Dense, tabular-looking, legible at large scale.

observed_font_evidence.role: humanist viewpoint, education, beauty, emotional keyword
clean modern body or business emphasis
editorial concept word and social observation
news, finance, concept, giant chapter word

maximum_text_length.exception: A two-line quote may exceed the soft limit only when the source effect is demonstrably readable at the target canvas.

density_targets.standard_talking_head: About 1-4% of text segments; usually one strong flower-text beat per 15-30 seconds.
density_targets.knowledge_payment_or_business: About 2-6%; prioritize hook, proof, method result, and CTA.
density_targets.high_packaging_or_yichuang: About 8-13%; vary font-only, background-card, and flower-text emphasis instead of making every hit identical.
density_targets.documentary_or_emotional: About 1-5%; prefer serif typography and restrained cinematic effects.

repetition_limits: Do not use one flower effect ID as the universal fallback.
Do not repeat the same flower effect on adjacent emphasis beats.
Use at most two flower-effect families in a short talking-head video unless the format is explicitly variety/high-packaging.
Prefer silence and plain typography over an effect that does not match the semantic beat.

talking_head_library.suggested_role: emotional story sentence; reuse only after visual verification
tutorial annotation; exclude from audience export by default

high_packaging_library.suggested_role: cinematic serif phrase, authority, question, result
internal tutorial label; exclude from audience export by default
temperature or numeric badge; low-confidence evidence
object or product keyword; low-confidence evidence
money desire or motivation; low-confidence evidence

text_shape_policy.rule: Treat text_shape as a separate background/label role, not as flower text. Do not stack text_shape, heavy flower text, and heavy motion on the same ordinary beat.

implementation_rules: Font file names are priorities, not proof that the font exists. Resolve an installed or existing draft font path and preserve the role when substituting.

Copying an effect_style_id alone is invalid. Create or reuse the matching materials.effects item, give it a fresh runtime id, attach that id through the text segment's extra_material_refs, and keep content.styles[*].effectStyle.id aligned with the source resource id.
When the exact effect resource cannot be resolved locally, do not invent a path or silently attach a broken effect. Use a portable typography fallback.
For partial keyword styling, compute character ranges from the final punctuation-cleaned text before writing content.styles.
Suppress duplicated base subtitles while a large overlay repeats the same phrase.
Preview at least the hook, first flower-text beat, densest overlay section, and ending.
quality_gate: Base captions remain readable without relying on the flower effect.
No more than three font families are used.
Flower-text density matches the selected output family.
Tutorial labels and source branding are filtered from audience-facing output.
Every attached font and effect resource resolves locally or has a deliberate fallback.
No unresolved material_id or extra_material_refs remain.
